question: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma is remembered for his mastery in playing ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Santoor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• P**andit Shivkumar Sharma** is remembered for his mastery in playing the **Santoor**, a musical instrument that originated in the **Kashmir Valley**.
 
• The Santoor is a type of **hammered dulcimer** that is played by striking the strings with a** pair of wooden m**allets.
 
• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma is credited with popularizing the Santoor as a **solo instrument** in Indian classical music.
 
• He has also collaborated with other musicians from different genres and countries, including the **Grateful Dead and the Kronos Quartet.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tabla:**

 
 
• The word "tabla" comes from the Arabic word "tabl," which denotes a drum or flat-surfaced instrument that faces upward.
 
• It serves as both a solo performance instrument and a crucial rhythmic accompaniment for solo and instrumental music ensembles.
 
 
 
• **Sarod:**
 
 
• The sarod is a plucked bowl-lute chordophone that is native to Pakistan and northern India.
 
• There is a small additional bridge next to the upper nut of the sarod type with eight main strings and two chikari strings.
 
• Four drone strings rest upon this bridge.
 
 
 
• **Sitar:**
 
 
• Hindustani classical music uses the sitar, a plucked stringed instrument from the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The sitar, which is typically four feet long and has a deep pear-shaped gourd body, features twenty arched movable frets, a long, wide, hollow wooden neck, and front and side tuning pegs.
